title.narrative: CAR- Public Sector Digital Governance Project

description.narrative: The Project Development objective (PDO) is: To (i) improve efficiency and transparency in key areas of public resources management, and (ii) lay foundations for a trusted and inclusive digital government.

The original project is an investment project in the amount of USD 35 million, based on four integrated and mutually reinforcing components. Component 1 (Improve the management of public resources) will build government capacity to improve performance in core public financial management and human resources functions, while streamlining procedures and leveraging digital technologies to increase financial controls, make more informed policy decisions and publish reliable information on the use of public resources. Component 2 (Digitally transform public administration and service delivery) will establish the foundational enabling environment for digital government, including supporting necessary legal and regulatory reforms. It will also aim at improving access to public services by supporting digital platforms and specific sector use cases like civil registration and identification. Component 3 (Citizen Engagement, Implementation support, and monitoring and evaluation [M&E]) will finance project management, communication, and M&E. Component 4 support a Contingent emergency response. The proposed additional financing aims to enhance mineral sector governance through digital data management, regulatory strengthening, and international transparency initiatives. Key activities include designing and installing a digitized geological and mineral information system (GMIS) to monitor and disseminate sector statistics via a public web-portal. The project will also convert existing paper-based reports and geological maps into digital formats, and acquire new geological data from remote sensing and limited soil sampling. Non-intrusive geological techniques such as ground-based geophysics, light-scale geochemical sampling, structural mapping, and remote sensing will be employed to update topographical mapping. This comprehensive data will help the government identify high-priority areas, attract investors, and inform land-use planning. Legal and regulatory advice will support drafting regulations to implement the Mining Code approved in August 2024. These activities aim to improve the investment climate and enhance regulatory oversight.The project is closely aligned with the objectives of the FY21-FY25 Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for CAR, and the National Recovery and Peace Consolidation plan (RCPCA, 2017-2023) as well as the principles of the Sustainable Development Goals (SGDs), and the World Bank Fragility, Conflict and Violence (FCV) Strategy. The project will build on ongoing public sector reforms currently supported by the WBG, while promoting collaboration with relevant WBG programs, and partners.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I, A, 2. The Recipient shall establish by no later than 1 month after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, an executive Secretariat chaired by representative from theministry in charge of finance representative from the state minister in charge of economy as vice-secretary and composed ofrepresentatives from ministries members of the PSC and the representative of the CSREF with terms of reference , composition,powers, functions, staffing, facilities and other resources satisfactory to the Association, to be responsible for providingtechnical support to the Project Steering Committee including inter alia overseeing the project, meeting at regular intervals toadopt relevant work programs and monitor their implementation, coordinate digitalization and PFM activities among donors, andmediate between beneficiary agencies.

Schedule 2, Section I, A, 3 (a). The Recipient shall maintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, a ProjectImplementation Unit (“PIU”), with terms of reference, composition, powers, functions, staffing, facilities and other resourcessatisfactory to the Association, to be responsible for the day to day implementation of the Project, including inter alia,environmental and social safeguards management, financial management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting.

Schedule 2, Section I, A, 3 (b). Without limiting the foregoing, the PIU shall include, inter alia, a Project coordinator, a chiefdigital governance officer, two technical coordinators, a financial management specialist, an accountant, a procurementspecialist,a procurement assistant, a monitoring and evaluation specialist, a social specialist, an assistant environmentalspecialist, a security specialist , communication specialist ; all with qualifications, experience, integrity and terms ofreference acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I, A, 3 (c). Without limiting the foregoing, not later than 3 months after the Effective Date, the Recipientshall have recruited and appointed a chief digital officer, two technical coordinators, a financial management specialist, aprocurement specialist, procurement assistant, monitoring and evaluation specialist, a security specialist, and a communicationspecialist, all with qualifications, experience, integrity and terms of reference acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I, A.1. The Recipient shall establish by no later than 1 month after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain at all times during the implementation of the Project, a Project Steering Committee, chaired by the minister in charge offinance, and the state minister in charge of economy and plan as vice-president and composed by representatives of relevantministries and with terms of reference, composition, powers, functions, staffing, facilities and other resources satisfactory tothe Association, to be responsible for inter alia, overseeing overall Project performance, approving Annual Work Plans and Budgets,providing strategic oversight and guidance, and supporting the mobilization of counterpart funds for the Project.

Schedule 2, Section I, B, 2 (b): The Recipient shall not later than November 30 of each year, furnish the draft annual work planand budget for the following year to the Association for its review, and promptly thereafter finalize the draft annual work planand budget, taking into account the Association's comments thereon; provided, that for the first year of Project implementation,the Recipient shall furnish the draft annual work plan and budget by no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date;

Schedule 2, Section I, C, 2 (a) and (b): The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient shallensure that: (a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligence and efficiency, as provided inthe ESCP.(b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP;

Schedule 2, Section I, C, 7: If 60 days prior to the Closing Date, the Association determines that there are measures and actionsspecified in the ESCP which will not be completed by the Closing Date, the Recipient shall: (a) not later than 30 days before theClosing Date, prepare and present to the Association, an action plan satisfactory to the Association on the outstanding measuresand actions, including a timetable and budget allocation for such measures and actions (which action plan shall deemed to beconsidered an amendment of the ESCP); and (b) thereafter, carry out said action plan in accordance with its terms and in a manneracceptable to the Association.
